title: PhysHanDI: Physics-Based Reconstruction of Hand-Deformable Object Interactions
claim: A physics-based interaction model couples hand and deformable object, and is fitted to real videos through staged reconstruction.
layout: 2 panels split by divider, left-to-right, big arrow linking model to learning stages
description: A wide figure split by a vertical divider into two titled panels. The left panel, 'Hand-Deformable Object Interaction Model (Sec. 3.1)', shows a rendered gray cloth mesh held by two MANO hands, labeled 'Deformable Object: Spring-Mass Model' and 'Hand: MANO Model'. A blue arrow leads to a rounded box, 'Interaction Modeling'. In the box, blue circles (hand vertices) connect through red zigzag virtual springs to yellow nodes (object nodes), with 'Force Transfer' written along the springs. A large gradient arrow, 'Fit the Model to Input RGB-D', points to the right panel, 'Learning from Sparse-View RGB-D Videos (Sec. 3.2)'. That panel has three stacked real video frames on the left and three blue boxes on the right: 1. Hand Reconstruction, 2. Object Reconstruction, 3. Hand Refinement. Downward arrows between the boxes carry the labels 'Interacting 3D Hands Prior' and 'Physics-Based Object Prior'.
caption: PhysHanDI models physically plausible hand–deformable object interactions. In our interaction model, each hand is represented by the MANO model [ref], and each object is represented by a spring–mass model [ref]. Their interaction is modeled by simulating object deformations driven by interaction forces derived from the reconstructed 3D hand motions. Our interaction model can be learned from sparse-view RGB-D videos through three stages: (1) hand reconstruction, (2) object reconstruction, and (3) hand refinement.
abstract: While existing methods for reconstructing hand-object interactions have made impressive progress, they either focus on rigid or part-wise rigid objects-limiting their ability to model real-world objects (e.g., cloth, stuffed animals) that exhibit highly non-rigid deformations-or model deformable objects without full 3D hand reconstruction. To bridge this gap, we present PhysHanDI (Physics-based Reconstruction of Hand and Deformable Object Interactions), a framework that enables full 3D reconstruction of both interacting hands and non-rigid objects. Our key idea is to physically simulate object deformations driven by forces induced from densely reconstructed 3D hand motions, ensuring that the reconstructed object dynamics are both physically plausible and coherent with the interacting hand movements. Furthermore, we demonstrate that such simulation of object deformations can, in turn, refine and improve hand reconstruction via inverse physics. In experiments, PhysHanDI outperforms the state-of-the-art baseline across reconstruction and future prediction.
